The current English and Chinese README examples already use `p002 --sites us uk`. Added a regression check that parses and builds those exact examples so the documentation cannot silently drift from the CLI again.

The targeted live P002 request using `--sites us` also succeeded: `20260905193854-0sgEwiPwA7yCWxgw` (this call additionally enabled one feature term and supplied an image).

See the [scoped verification report](https://github.com/SuntekCorps-xLab/eric-compliance-suite/blob/main/reports/2026-09-05-live-verification.md) for request evidence, actual recorded costs, and untested boundaries.

The earlier closure was automatic from the merge commit; this comment adds the missing resolution and validation follow-up.

Added Bash/zsh and Windows PowerShell token setup instructions in both README languages, SKILL.md, and the missing-token CLI error. PowerShell users now get:

```powershell
$env:ERIC_API_TOKEN = "your-api-token"
```

For persistence, `setx ERIC_API_TOKEN "your-api-token"` is documented separately with the requirement to open a new terminal. The current-session command takes effect immediately. The missing-token recovery output is covered by regression tests, including the Windows/Python 3.12 CI job; tests do not print real credentials.

README and SKILL.md now explain that a visible chat attachment is usable only when the agent runtime exposes readable bytes/a local file. When it does not, the instructions and CLI recovery text explain how to provide a saved local path or a public image URL.

URL downloading was already implemented. It was verified separately against a public sample image: the CLI downloader returned bytes with the same SHA-256 as the local copy. Real C001, L001 and P001 checks also accepted the downloaded local images. No claim is made that the skill can extract bytes from a visual-only attachment.

Aligned the copyright reference and Skill with C001's integrated `enable_radar` request, `similarity`, `copyright_code`, and `sub_radar_result`. The CLI normalizes numeric and legacy string radar values, and a positive item radar result contributes to the displayed high-risk classification.

Live request `20260905192955-G59GEMpsoiB0diPH` returned `data.radar_result = 1` and item radar values `[1, 0, 0]`. The response used the documented current field names and replayed successfully through the normal renderer. Offline regression cases separately verify low similarity plus positive radar, zero/null/unknown values, and `--no-radar`. The live call was confirmed in the deduction ledger at 2 points.

Added local checks for documented text lengths, region/site values, numeric ranges, JSON shapes, required option combinations, and nonempty inputs before any HTTP request.

The follow-up live test found an additional missing combination: P002 feature detection requires an image. Request `20260905193733-6knRs4VTP5CVrTln` was rejected with `4000001 feature_detect.features.image不能为空`; its measured point balance did not change. This is fixed in the follow-up commit: `--enable-feature` now requires both feature IDs and a nonempty `--feature-image`, and missing/whitespace images exit locally with code 2. Added a regression test and corrected the reference/README/Skill.

With an image supplied, `20260905193854-0sgEwiPwA7yCWxgw` succeeded and the measured debit was 7 points for one feature term.

All commands now keep the original API JSON alone on stdout, send human-readable notices to stderr, exit nonzero for API failures, and label locally calculated billing values as estimates. A failed response never prints the successful-completion estimate.

The shared response handler was exercised against the real NL rejection `20260905193151-Anx4vVEvmbbxH9xZ`: `success=false`, code `4000001`, valid standalone JSON, exit code 1, and no completion notice. The rejected P002 request `20260905193733-6knRs4VTP5CVrTln` also preserved error JSON; a before/after balance check showed zero debit for that particular request. The CLI still does not infer that every failure is free or query the account ledger itself.

Added `--dry-run` to all 12 commands. It validates inputs, builds the same live request payload including image encoding, and emits the URL, redacted authentication header, estimated live cost, and `points_consumed: 0`. It does not require a token or make network requests.

Offline tests cover every command and compare preview payloads with those passed to the live transport. Offline image URLs are rejected before downloading so the zero-network contract holds; use local files/base64. README also documents the older macOS LibreSSL/urllib3 warning and using a maintained OpenSSL-backed Python installation.

Added and documented two zero-point integration paths for all commands:

- `--dry-run` validates request construction and shows the target URL, complete payload, token-presence flag and redacted header.
- `--mock-response FILE` exercises normal response rendering from a local API envelope or a sequence of envelopes, including T002 follow-ups. Exhausting the fixture sequence never falls back to a live call.

The offline guide includes expected request JSON, a sample image, representative C001/P001 responses and an error fixture. Both modes work without a token or third-party site packages and are covered by offline tests. These modes verify local wiring; token validity and server acceptance require separate live checks, whose scoped results are now recorded in the verification report.
